MAINT-TIMEOUT-S1.title: Define Timeout State Schema and UX Contract
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S1.description: Define frontend state model for long-running requests including timeout threshold, modal visibility, retry state, aborted request flags, and idempotent resume behavior. Establish contract for continue vs abandon behavior including state persistence across re-renders.

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S2.title: Implement Timeout Detection and Retry Logic
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S2.description: Implement core logic using timers and AbortController to detect long-running requests (~45s), trigger timeout state, and manage request lifecycle with a unique requestId for idempotent resume. Ensure continue action does not duplicate backend calls or UI messages, and abandon safely cancels and cleans up pending promises and state.

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S3.title: Build Timeout Modal UI and User Actions
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S3.description: Implement timeout modal with clear messaging and actions: Continue waiting or Abandon request. Ensure proper UX state transitions, accessibility (focus trap, keyboard actions), and message continuity without disrupting chat history.

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S4.title: Unit Tests for Timeout and Abort Scenarios
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S4.description: Create unit tests for timeout trigger timing, AbortController cancellation, retry/continue flows, requestId correlation, and state transitions including edge cases (rapid user actions, duplicate prevention, unmounted component cleanup).

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S5.title: End-to-End Integration of Timeout UX Flow
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S5.description: Validate full flow from user message submission through long-running backend response, timeout modal display, user decision (continue/abandon), and final UI state consistency ensuring no duplicate responses, no orphaned requests, and correct reconciliation of late-arriving responses.
